newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador president to be tried for slander.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador president to be tried for slander.

text.p: Ecuadoran President Abdala Bucaram was formally notified on Monday that the country's highest court will try him on charges of injurious slander brought by his rival in the 1996 presidential election.

"The lawsuit presented by Jaime Nebot against Abdala Bucaram is clear, comprehensive, and meets all of the formal requisites," Supreme Court of Justice president Carlos Solorzano said in his written decision to accept the case.
Nebot is the leader of the Social Christian Party (PSC), the main political opposition force in Ecuador, and was its unsuccessful presidential candidate in 1996.

He lodged an accusation of "injurious slander" against Bucaram with the supreme court shortly after Bucaram alleged Nebot had "appropriated for himself" some $5 million during a highway construction project in Guayaquil.
After giving Bucaram formal notification of the trial, Solorzano gave him six working days, beginning on Monday, to reply to the charges.

Should he be unable to prove his graft allegations against Nebot, Bucaram theoretically faces a possible six-month to two-year prison sentence, plus payment of compensatory damages in an amount determined by the court.
Ecuadoran law also says, however, that the president can be impeached for only treason and or corruption, leaving the current case against Bucaram in murky legal waters.

Bucaram, who proudly calls himself "El Loco" (The Crazy One) and was sworn in five months ago, boasted during his presidential campaign that during his lifetime he has had to respond to some 30 lawsuits.
